English · 한국어

easy-session

Click through the line above the input and the session panel · 0.1.31

easy-session lets you turn Claude Code features like the advisor and ultrathink on and off right from the line above the input, and shows when the advisor was called, what Claude did around it, and what it cost. Reports from sessions you opened wait until you choose to take them, instead of waking your session. As sessions add up, it keeps them in order with roles like main and orchestrator, and a session tree.

Topic by topic

①On and off with a click, and in view

UsuallyPeople often keep the thinking depth (effort) set high. The level you set stays for later sessions [3], so light turns get deep thinking too. Turning the advisor on or off means typing /advisor, and finding when it was called means scrolling back through the conversation [1]. What it cost is a separate look with /usage [1].

With easy-sessionLeave effort as it is and press ultrathink only for the turns that need deep thinking. In the desktop app’s Code tab that turn runs at xhigh while your session effort stays the same [3]. Turn the advisor on and off above the input, with when it was called, what came before and after, the count and the cost in view.

②Reports go up only when you choose

UsuallyWhen a session opens a new session, the desktop app puts that session’s report into the one that opened it each time it ends a turn. If the opener was idle, it runs a turn to read each report, and each of those turns uses tokens.

With easy-sessionReports are held and managed on their own. Turns that carry only a report are stopped, and in Now or the Below tile you view, take, delete, or take all of them. You see what one request costs when you take them, and taking only the ones you pick means fewer wake-up turns and fewer tokens.

③>> — easy-session’s own command

UsuallyTo pass an answer to another session, you ask once more after it arrives: “send this to main”. That request is a turn too.

With easy-sessionEnd your message with >>up or >>main and the answer goes to the session above or the main when the turn ends. ➤ sends just your text, without a turn.

④Managing sessions

UsuallyAs sessions add up, you settle in words which session splits the work and which does it, open sessions one by one to see what’s going on, and write handover notes by hand.

With easy-sessionRoles (Main · Orchestrator · Sub · Solo) and the session tree sit in one panel. One press of Hand over lets the next round take over the place, the sessions below, the pin and the board, and sending to an ended session asks first.

Install

Send Claude this one line (in the desktop app’s Code tab or a terminal session).

Install this plugin: github.com/JaeSeongHa5280/easy-session (claude plugin marketplace add JaeSeongHa5280/easy-session, then claude plugin install easy-session@easy-session)

Then quit the Claude app completely and open it again (or start a new claude session). The Session panel button appears on the line above the input.

To type it yourself, send each line on its own in Claude’s input box.

/plugin marketplace add JaeSeongHa5280/easy-session

/plugin install easy-session@easy-session

Good to know

  • Permission modes matter. Buttons that change the app (pin, archive, detach, export, Remote Control, send) act directly only in a session running in Bypass permissions. In other modes they put a one-line request in your input, and it happens when you send it. In auto mode the desktop app hands an app tool called by a plugin’s own code back, asking for Claude to make the call (an app rule, checked on Claude Code 2.1.325). This mock is a Bypass permissions session.
  • VS Code and terminal sessions get the line above the input and the session panel too. They sit outside the desktop app’s session tree, so the Pin and Forward items and the Above · Siblings · Below tiles are dimmed or left out, and sending happens in the session panel.
  • The screen language is Settings → Screen · advisor → 언어 · Language (Auto · 한국어 · English). Some forms stay Korean in English too: a handover is recognized when the new session’s title is the next round (… 4차 → … 5차).
  • Dollar amounts are rough estimates at fixed per-token rates. On a subscription, read them as how heavy a request is.
